- changelog.d/5809-duplicate-check-trusted-target-and-fix.md: line 16, the "For contributors" subsection, last sentence
  severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The new refusal tests (`test_member_and_collaborator_targets_and_fixes_are_trusted`, `test_untrusted_target_or_fix_blocks_the_close`, `test_the_finding_scenario_is_not_eligible`, `test_same_repository_check_ignores_case`, `test_an_untrusted_target_gives_no_evidence`) and the `_target`/`_fix` fixture updates live in `tests/test_permission_prompt_duplicates.py` (diff hunks tests/test_permission_prompt_duplicates.py:419-451 and 543-610). The PR description's own "Evidence" table names `tests/test_permission_prompt_duplicates.py`; `tests/test_permission_prompts.py` carries only `test_template_parity` (byte-identity between the twin and the workflow-templates copy).
  WHY: A maintainer following the changelog to locate the refusal coverage would open `tests/test_permission_prompts.py`, find only the parity test, and conclude the new refusal behaviour is undocumented at the test layer. The sentence should read `tests/test_permission_prompt_duplicates.py`.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py and .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: `decide_duplicate_close`, the line `target_markers = _outside_fenced_examples(str(target.get("body") or "")) if target_trusted else ""` (and the symmetric helper call)
  severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Type inconsistency. When `target_trusted` is True, `target_markers` is the return value of `_outside_fenced_examples(...)` (a list in the original code path). When False, it is the empty string `""`. The same name holds either a list or a `str`.
  WHY: Today the downstream code is forgiving enough that `test_an_untrusted_target_gives_no_evidence` passes — empty string and empty list are both falsy and iterable-via-`in`. Any future code that does indexing, slicing, or method calls (e.g. `target_markers.append(...)`, `len(target_markers[0])`) would silently differ between the two paths or break on the untrusted path. The robust equivalent is `target_markers = ... if target_trusted else []` (matching type) or `target_markers = ... if target_trusted else _outside_fenced_examples("")` (consistent parsing). Either change is a one-line tweak in each of the two files.
- agents.md: the inserted block at lines 1199-1201 ("An untrusted M also leaves the `target_class` and `target_occurrences` evidence `null` …")
  severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Indentation/style drift. The new paragraph is indented 2 spaces and is inserted after a blank line that closes the preceding bulleted list; the next paragraph (`/implement-issue-claude` step 5a runs it ...) is at 3 spaces, and the list items above are at 2-4 spaces. The same diff also slips two new bullets (`M is another issue, open or closed as completed, by an owner, member, or collaborator`; `P is a same-repository PR …`) into the existing list without a separating blank line, so the list-then-paragraph boundary is now mixed.
  WHY: Not a runtime defect. A documentation-rendering concern — strict CommonMark parsers may handle the list/paragraph indent mix differently than GitHub's flavour, and a future maintainer copy-pasting the bullets might see the list as a single run-on paragraph.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: lines 943-944 (the inline comment in `decide_duplicate_close`)
  severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The executable `.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py` retains the old misleading comment:
```
# A fork PR, or one by an account without write access, is no verified fix,
# and only such a PR's title, body, and branch name bind it to the target.
```
while the twin `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py` has the corrected 5-line comment at lines 943-947:
```
# Issue #5809: only a same-repository PR whose `author_association` is in
# FIX_CLAIM_TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR) counts as a
# verified fix; a fork PR or one by any other author does not. That is a trust
# policy, not a write-permission check. The title, body, and branch-name
# reference checked below binds a PR to the target only when it passes both.
```
The files differ by exactly 3 lines (1034 vs 1037 total), matching the 2-line to 5-line comment change. The last commit (`05a3876`, "[claude-twin-sync] permission_prompts.py review round 1 for #5809") was supposed to sync this fix, but the `.claude/` copy still has the old comment.
  WHY: `tests/test_permission_prompts.py:374` asserts `TEMPLATE_SCRIPT_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == SCRIPT_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")` — a byte-for-byte comparison of the twin and the executable copy. With the comment mismatch, this test fails deterministically. The old comment is also factually misleading: it calls the `author_association` check a "write access" check (it is a trust-set membership check — MEMBER/COLLABORATOR may have read/triage-only permissions), and "only such a PR" grammatically refers to the rejected fork/untrusted PR rather than the accepted trusted same-repository PR, inverting the intended meaning.
